definitions.explanation: A person whose behavior, habits, or thinking is notably unusual or unconventional. Can be used with mild affection or amusement.

examples.japanese: あの{教授|きょうじゅ}は{奇人|きじん}で{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: That professor is famous for being an eccentric.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{奇人|きじん}だが、{仕事|しごと}の{腕|うで}は{確|たし}かだ。
examples.english: He's an oddball, but his work skills are solid.

examples.japanese: {町|まち}には{昔|むかし}から{奇人|きじん}{変人|へんじん}と{呼|よ}ばれる{人物|じんぶつ}が{何人|なんにん}かいた。
examples.english: The town has always had a few people who were called eccentrics and oddballs.

notes:
Composed of {奇|き} (strange, unusual) + {人|じん} (person). Often used as part of the set phrase {奇人|きじん}{変人|へんじん} (eccentrics and oddballs), which is a common four-character expression.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {奇人|きじん}{変人|へんじん} (eccentrics and oddballs — often used as a pair)
- {奇人|きじん}と{呼|よ}ばれる (to be called an eccentric)
- {奇人|きじん}で{有名|ゆうめい} (famous as an eccentric)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {変人|へんじん} — weirdo, odd person (slightly more negative than {奇人|きじん})
- {変|へん}わり{者|もの} — unconventional person, nonconformist (milder, can be positive)
- {風変|ふうが}わり — peculiar, eccentric (na-adjective describing the quality itself)
